description: Machine-readable inventory of React audit checks for validation and generated maps.

statusTaxonomy.present: The expected invariant is fully satisfied.
statusTaxonomy.partial: Most signals resolve, with a small number of exceptions, or the codebase shows mixed adherence to a soft check.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns performance-driven memoization and rendering cost; this audit owns correctness-driven memoization.
Owns module boundaries and global state strategy; state-management checks overlap.
Owns the eslint-plugin-react-hooks configuration this audit expects.

checks.title: eslint-plugin-react-hooks recommended set enabled
checks.expectation: The hooks plugin's recommended rules are enabled in the active ESLint configuration, or the equivalent Biome rules for Biome projects.
checks.violationSignal: The plugin is missing or the recommended set is off.

checks.title: No silenced exhaustive-deps without justification
checks.expectation: exhaustive-deps disable lines carry a justification comment on the same or adjacent line.
checks.violationSignal: Suppressions of exhaustive-deps with no surrounding explanation.

checks.title: No empty dependency arrays where dependencies exist
checks.expectation: An empty useEffect dependency array is not used when the body closes over rendered values that change.
checks.violationSignal: Effects with empty dependency arrays that read varying state, props, or context.

checks.title: No data fetching in effects when a query library exists
checks.expectation: When a query library or framework loader is available, components fetch via the data layer rather than useEffect plus fetch.
checks.violationSignal: useEffect calling fetch or axios in a project with a query layer installed.

checks.title: No state synchronisation
checks.expectation: State is derived from props or other state rather than stored in useState and re-synchronised by useEffect.
checks.violationSignal: A useEffect that does setX(propX) to mirror props into state.

checks.title: Status enums over multiple booleans
checks.expectation: Multi-stage state uses a single status enum rather than separate booleans that can drift.
checks.violationSignal: Three or more boolean state variables representing a single conceptual lifecycle.

checks.title: useRef for mutable non-render state
checks.expectation: Mutable values that do not trigger re-renders use useRef, not useState.
checks.violationSignal: useState used to hold a value never read in render but mutated frequently.

checks.title: Cleanup functions present for side effects
checks.expectation: useEffect returns a cleanup for subscriptions, timers, observers, async cancellation, and event listeners.
checks.violationSignal: Side-effect setup with no matching teardown.

checks.title: Memoization for correctness, not just performance
checks.expectation: Callbacks or values in a downstream hook's dependency array that need referential stability for correctness are wrapped in useCallback or useMemo.
checks.violationSignal: A useEffect whose dependencies include an inline callback created on each render.

checks.title: Custom hook design
checks.expectation: Custom hooks have a single responsibility, are named useFoo, and return a consistent shape across the codebase.
checks.violationSignal: Custom hooks returning mixed shapes inconsistently, or named without the use prefix.

checks.title: Function components only in new code
checks.expectation: New components are function components; class components persist only as legacy.
checks.violationSignal: Class components are present, and especially a class component newer than the most recent function component.

checks.title: Components named in PascalCase
checks.expectation: Component files and exported component identifiers use PascalCase.
checks.violationSignal: Non-PascalCase component definitions.

checks.title: Hooks named with use prefix
checks.expectation: Custom hooks export identifiers starting with use followed by an uppercase letter.
checks.violationSignal: A function that calls hooks but does not start with use.

checks.title: forwardRef for ref-receiving components
checks.expectation: Components that need to receive ref use forwardRef, or React 19 ref-as-prop.
checks.violationSignal: A component renders a focusable element consumers would ref, but does not forward refs and is not React-19 ref-as-prop.

checks.title: displayName on memo and forwardRef wrappers
checks.expectation: Components wrapped in React.memo or forwardRef set displayName so the DevTools tree is readable.
checks.violationSignal: Wrapped components with no displayName.

checks.title: Children prop typed
checks.expectation: When a component accepts children, the prop is typed React.ReactNode.
checks.violationSignal: children: any or children: JSX.Element in component prop types.

checks.title: One component or hook per file
checks.expectation: Files export one primary component or hook plus supporting types and helpers.
checks.violationSignal: Files exporting more than three independent components or hooks.

checks.title: Named exports for components
checks.expectation: Components are exported as named exports, not default exports.
checks.violationSignal: Default-exported components in projects that otherwise use named exports.

checks.title: Form state via a form library
checks.expectation: Forms with more than five fields or non-trivial validation use a dedicated form library.
checks.violationSignal: Complex forms hand-rolled with a useState per field.

checks.title: Server state in the data layer
checks.expectation: Server-fetched data lives in a data layer rather than component-local useState populated by useEffect plus fetch.
checks.violationSignal: Fetched-data state held in component state with no query layer involved.

checks.title: Single global state library
checks.expectation: Exactly one global state strategy is used as the application's global state approach.
checks.violationSignal: Multiple global state libraries in the same application.

checks.title: No state synchronisation between sources of truth
checks.expectation: Data is stored in one place and derived elsewhere, not duplicated across component state, a global store, and a URL parameter at once.
checks.violationSignal: Detected duplicate-state patterns.

checks.title: State at the right level
checks.expectation: Local state lives where it is used, lifted state at the lowest common ancestor, and global state only for genuinely global concerns.
checks.violationSignal: Global state holding single-subtree values, or local state for values used across the application.

checks.title: URL state for shareable or recoverable state
checks.expectation: Search queries, filters, sort orders, current page, and selected tabs live in URL parameters when the user expects them to survive a reload.
checks.violationSignal: Patterns where a refresh would lose UI state the user expects to keep.

checks.title: useId for accessible IDs
checks.expectation: Generated IDs used to wire up labels, ARIA attributes, and form controls use useId.
checks.violationSignal: Hand-rolled ID generation when React 18+ is available.

checks.title: useTransition or startTransition for non-urgent updates
checks.expectation: Deferrable updates use useTransition or startTransition.
checks.violationSignal: Detected hot patterns where transitions would help and are absent.

checks.title: Suspense boundaries for async data
checks.expectation: When the framework or library supports Suspense for data fetching, Suspense boundaries with meaningful fallbacks are used.
checks.violationSignal: Async data fetched without surrounding Suspense in projects that opted into Suspense-based fetching.

checks.title: 'use client' used minimally and deliberately
checks.expectation: Client-component boundaries sit at the leaves of the tree, not at the root.
checks.violationSignal: Excessive 'use client' fragmentation, or 'use client' files importing server-only modules.
checks.skipWhenAbsent: The Next.js App Router is not in use.

checks.title: Server Actions used appropriately
checks.expectation: Mutating operations in App Router projects use Server Actions when appropriate.
checks.violationSignal: Patterns where Server Actions would be the natural choice but route handlers are used instead.
checks.skipWhenAbsent: The Next.js App Router is not in use.

checks.title: useOptimistic for optimistic mutations
checks.expectation: Optimistic UI updates use useOptimistic rather than hand-rolled optimistic state.
checks.violationSignal: Hand-rolled optimistic updates in React 19 codebases.
checks.skipWhenAbsent: The project is on React 18.x rather than React 19.
